rule: Each marker (a colour occurring exactly once) starts a one-cell-wide 8-connected line of its path colour. The line counts as continuing across any ring it touches (resuming from another contact of that ring) and across a single crossing cell of another marker's path. Every ring touched by that connected line has its enclosed background pocket filled with the marker colour. Rings touched only by disconnected or marker-less lines stay empty.

authored_scope: Random scenes: sides 10..30 by default (8..30 explicit), with random background (mostly 0). There are 1..3 markers, each with its own path colour and 1..4 threaded rings. Ring pockets are rectangles, thin bars or bent polyominoes, and about 20% are clipped by one grid edge on purpose. Ring jumps go through corners or contacts. Lines are shortest paths that sometimes detour via a waypoint. Optional features: tails, marker blobs, a single marker-on-marker crossing (orthogonal or diagonal, sides >= 12, sparser ring budget), untouched distractor rings, a marker-less distractor line in a fresh colour or the same colour as a marker path, and decoy colours appearing 2..3 times. Sizes above the fixture range are a synthetic extension. Not supported: rings sharing walls, path cells replacing ring walls, wide or irregular path bodies (test 2's 9 structure), slanted pockets, crossings with the marker-less line, multiple crossings. Fixtures are replayed from explicit input grids plus latent pocket fill seeds, not from a solver.
authored_constraints: Ring footprints are separated by Chebyshev distance >= 3 and never trap outside background cells.
Every ring's pocket is a background 4-component whose in-grid orthogonal border is the single ring colour; clipped rings use the grid edge as one side.
Each line touches exactly its assigned rings (8-adjacency check after drawing).
Lines are one cell wide. Waypoint detours forbid the second leg from touching the first. The crossing approach may only touch mid1 through pre.
Each marker's 8-neighbourhood contains only background and its own path colour, which must appear there.
Marker colours are exactly the singleton colours. The decoy colour appears 2..3 times. No non-background colour reaches the background count.
Any extra single-colour enclosure must be of a line colour and must not be reachable by a different marker's line.
Crossings are only built when both sides are >= 12, and use a ring budget of w*h/60.
Integer controls reject bools and non-integers. Flag controls must be bool or None. rings_per_marker must be a list or tuple of ints.
Construction is bounded: 500 attempts, each with bounded placement, waypoint and BFS work.

original_audit.rule: Rings are closed outlines; each 4-encloses a pocket of background, and the grid edge may close one side. A marker is a colour that occurs exactly once. A one-cell-wide, 8-connected line of a path colour leaves the marker. The line can resume across a ring, where only ring wall lies between the two parts. It can also resume across a single crossing cell of another marker's line. Every ring that the marker-connected line 8-touches has its pocket filled with the marker colour. Same-colour line segments not connected to a marker leave their rings empty. Colours occurring 2-3 times are not markers. Nothing else changes.

findings.location: _crossing_site / _site_ok: `if q in body and (k in (0, 4) or q not in allowed)` with site = x + k*e, a = x - d, b = x + d
findings.issue: The docstring says the crossing may be any direction not parallel to the crossed stretch. The geometry contradicts this. (1) Diagonal stretch d=(±1,±1) crossed by an orthogonal e: one of pre-a, pre-b, post-a, post-b is always ±2e±d, which has Chebyshev norm 1. So pre or post is always 8-adjacent to a or b, and every such site is rejected. Orthogonal-through-diagonal crossings can never be generated. (2) Orthogonal stretch d=(0,1) crossed by a diagonal e=(1,1): mid1=(x0-1,x1-1) is adjacent to route[i-2] unless that cell is (x0+1,x1-2), and mid2 needs route[i+2]=(x0-1,x1+2). So this case only appears when the crossed line has a specific S-bend. In practice the only reachable crossings are perpendicular orthogonal/orthogonal and diagonal/diagonal. Test 1's crossing, where the vertical 3-line cuts the diagonal 1-line at rows 6-7, cols 24-26, is the unreachable orthogonal-through-diagonal type.
findings.suggested_fix: Option A: narrow the docstring to perpendicular crossings. Option B: when d is diagonal and e is orthogonal, allow pre and post to neighbour exactly a or b, mirroring how mid1 and mid2 are allowed. Also relax the route[i±2] restriction for diagonal-on-orthogonal crossings. Then re-run the uniqueness and reference checks.
findings.test: Call generate(crossing=True, num_markers=2, width=30, height=30) about 200 times. Locate the crossing as the path-colour cell whose two opposite 8-neighbours carry the other path colour. Classify the crossed stretch and the crossing line as orthogonal or diagonal. Prediction: zero cases of a diagonal stretch crossed orthogonally, and diagonal-crossing-orthogonal is rare.

findings.location: _attempt plan loop: `blocked = all_foot | _dilate(placed, 1, ...)` applied to the distractor line when `same` is true
findings.issue: The same-colour distractor line only has to stay at Chebyshev distance 2 or more from marker lines. It can therefore run parallel to, or end exactly one background cell from, the marker's line of the same colour. In this task, gaps in a line are legitimate at rings and crossings. A one-cell plain gap between two same-colour segments is visually close to a continuation. The intended answer ('disconnected, leave empty') then depends on a fine detail that no fixture tests. The fixtures' disconnected segments in train 1 and test 1 are several cells away.
findings.suggested_fix: When `same` is true, block `_dilate(cells_of_same_colour_lines, 3)` for the distractor line, not radius 1. Optionally require the gap to be at least 2 background cells in every direction.
findings.test: Call generate(distractor_same_colour=True, num_distractor_rings=2, width=20, height=20) about 100 times. Compute the minimum Chebyshev distance between the marker-connected component of the path colour and the other component of the same colour. Report how often it equals 2.

findings.location: generate: `if needed > _budget(max_w, max_h, bool(crossing))` with _budget = w*h//40 (max 22 at 30x30), followed by `for _ in range(500): _attempt(...)`
findings.issue: The budget assumes about 40 cells per ring. A typical rounded ring has a 4x4 footprint plus a 2-cell exclusion margin, so random placement realistically fits about half of 22 rings on 30x30, before any line routing. Inputs such as rings_per_marker=[10,10,2] pass validation but probably exhaust 500 attempts. Each attempt runs up to 22x80 placement tries with _traps and _dilate. The likely outcome is a slow RuntimeError rather than a ValueError.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more conservative budget, such as w*h//70, or cap the per-marker and total ring counts. Fail fast with ValueError when the request is near the cap.
findings.test: Run generate(rings_per_marker=[10, 10, 2], width=30, height=30) once, under a host timeout. Record whether it succeeds, how long it takes, and which exception it raises.

findings.issue: The documented range is 0..40, but the budget check caps needed rings at 22 at 30x30. Any num_distractor_rings of 22 or more is always rejected. The advertised upper bound is unreachable.
findings.suggested_fix: Set _MAX_DISTRACTOR_RINGS to the real budget-derived ceiling, or document the dependence on grid size.

findings.location: _ring_shape polyomino branch: random-walk `cand` with size up to 10; `_extra_enclosure` only looks for enclosed cells that are not in pocket|wall
findings.issue: An 8-cell annulus (3x3 minus its centre) is a reachable random-walk polyomino. Its centre is a 4-neighbour of the pocket, so it becomes a wall cell. That gives an isolated ring-colour pillar inside the pocket, which _extra_enclosure does not flag. The fill stays correct, but this ring morphology has no counterpart in the fixtures.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject polyominoes with any wall cell that is not 4-connected (through wall cells) to the outer wall. A simpler alternative is to reject any wall cell whose four 4-neighbours are all pocket.
findings.test: Over many _ring_shape() draws, count shapes with a wall cell that has all four 4-neighbours in the pocket. Prediction: the count is non-zero.

findings.issue: Replay does not check grid size (1..30), cell values (0..9), the structure of `fills` entries, or whether a fill colour equals the background or ring colour. For example, fills=[(1,1,0)] on a background-0 pocket is a silent no-op.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate dimensions, the cell value range, `fills` as 3-int sequences, and that the fill colour differs from both the background and the pocket's border colour.
findings.test: generate(input_grid=[[0,2,0],[2,0,2],[0,2,0]], fills=[[1,1,0]]) currently succeeds with output equal to input. It should arguably raise.

findings.location: validate(): replay with hand-written fill seeds
findings.issue: The fixture replay flood-fills seeds that already encode the answer. It never runs the generator's routing logic or any rule-based solver. I hand-traced all 24 seeds against the canonical outputs and each names the correct single-colour pocket. However, this only shows the seeds are right, not that the generator matches the rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the replay, but add a host-side check that runs the reference transform on random generator output.
findings.test: For 200 default samples, check reference transform(input) == output, with the checkpoint-emitting calls stubbed out.

targeted_checks: Run the reference transform (with emit stubbed) on generator outputs across defaults, crossing=True, distractor_same_colour=True, marker_blob=True, decoy=True and background!=0. Require exact equality.
Invariant: input and output differ only on pocket cells, each changed pocket uses a single marker colour, and every marker colour occurs exactly once in the input.
Invariant: no non-background colour other than the markers occurs exactly once, and decoy colours occur 2-3 times.
Histogram of crossing geometry (crossed stretch orthogonal or diagonal vs crossing line orthogonal or diagonal) under crossing=True.
Minimum gap between a same-colour distractor component and the marker-connected component.
Confirm common.grid(width, height, bg) returns height rows of width cells, especially for width=10, height=30.
Confirm the reference `components()` helper is 4-connected. With 8-connectivity, rounded-corner pockets leak diagonally into the outside and no holes are found.
Time the near-budget inputs, e.g. rings_per_marker=[10,10,2] at 30x30, under a timeout.
Count polyomino rings that contain an interior wall pillar.
scope_limits: No code was executed. All needs_execution findings are hypotheses.

The reference prose says path cells 'replace part of the ring's border'. In the fixtures, path cells sit on the rounded-corner positions, e.g. train 1 (3,19), (3,22), (13,6), (13,9). The generator's choice to forbid wall replacement matches the fixtures, not the prose.

The reference prose for test 2 suggests the 5-ring may stay empty. The canonical output fills it with 4, because the 1-path connects through the 8-ring wall at rows 2-5, cols 17-20. The prose's '8-rings' filled with 4 is also overstated: only one 8-ring gets 4. These are prose issues, not generator defects. No fixture corrections are proposed.
Test 2's wide or irregular 9-body path, test 1's slanted parallelogram pocket, and test 1's two-cell non-collinear crossing are explicitly out of the generator's scope.
This report is not approval for registration.
